The tests-quality auditor observed gate-ui.mjs change under it mid-audit and flagged a concurrent editor. watchOrigin LATCHES everDown on a SINGLE failed 4s sample with no confirmation, and assessRun then VOIDs the run. A Vite dev server serving 6 concurrent Chromium pages routinely exceeds 4s on a cold transform, so one slow sample out of ~144 discards a healthy 12-minute crawl — a FALSE FAIL, the exact failure mode this module claims to eliminate.

contaminationOf counts request-failures that isHarnessNoise ALREADY classifies as benign routine-reload noise, and divides by findings.length INCLUDING LOW spacing-grid items. So a run can be 0-gating-HIGH and simultaneously VOID (false FAIL), while a run with 10k LOW findings can hide 900 real transport errors under the 10% bar (false PASS). origin/main's own baseline is 36/608 = 5.9%, uncomfortably near the bar. Corroborated by the tests-quality angle independently.

The lock's liveness proof is the HOLDER's pid, but the process that crawls is a spawnSync CHILD. SIGKILL gate-ui and the child is reparented and keeps crawling for ~12 min; the next acquirer sees a dead holder pid, reclaims, and starts a SECOND concurrent crawl — precisely the corruption the lock exists to prevent, now blessed as a 'stale reclaim'.

Registering SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP suppresses Node's default terminate, and gate-ui blocks the event loop in spawnSync for the whole crawl, so the handler cannot run. gate:ui becomes UNKILLABLE by SIGTERM for ~12 minutes where it previously died instantly — the signal handling buys nothing in the only window it matters and costs the ability to stop a wedged run. Empirically verified by the auditor (6s of ignored SIGTERM in a minimal repro).

tryCreate is atomic for EXISTENCE but not CONTENT: openSync('wx') creates a zero-byte file before writeSync fills it. A concurrent acquirer reading in that window gets null, judges the record 'unreadable', unlinks the winner's brand-new lock and takes its own — two simultaneous holders. The 'corrupt must never wedge' policy is what turns the write window into a mutual-exclusion hole.

Stale reclaim is a read-then-unlink TOCTOU: it never verifies the file still holds the record it judged stale, so two waiters (which wake within the same second after a holder dies) can both reclaim, the second deleting the first's freshly created lock.

Liveness is pid-only and alive() counts EPERM as alive, so a recycled pid makes a dead run's lock look valid for up to MAX_HOLD_MS = 2 HOURS, wedging every gate:ui on the host (each waiting its 15-minute budget then exiting 2).

The host lock wraps the ENTIRE gate (tsc, lint, crawl, Playwright visual), not just the crawl that needs serialization. With a 15-minute wait budget the THIRD concurrent gate:ui is guaranteed to hard-fail with exit 2 — indistinguishable in a pipeline from a genuine gate failure, converting a throughput problem into a false FAIL.

RUNTIME_FINDINGS.md — the artifact CLAUDE.md points humans at — is written BEFORE the void check, carries no void banner, and is NOT removed by clearRunArtifacts. So a VOID run publishes contaminated data under a 'gate-failing' heading, and a KILLED run leaves the previous run's md in place: the stale-inheritance defect this feature exists to close, left open on the one artifact a human reads.

The crash-mute's corroboration is only 'this cell also saw ANY dev-asset transport failure' — and a dev-asset ERR_ABORTED is documented routine noise (36 in the origin/main baseline). So a REAL broken dynamic import in a cell that also produced one routine abort is muted and the surface reports PASS while rendering nothing but an ErrorBoundary. This is the first time a crash can be muted and the corroborating evidence is harness-generated: an INV-1 blindness introduced by the fix.

The `inherited` branch returns silently, contradicting the file's own 'never returns silently-unlocked' contract. GATE_UI_LOCK_TOKEN is a plain env var: once exported into a shell, EVERY gate:ui skips the lock with zero output and two runs overlap exactly as before. Nothing validates the token against a live holder.

eachValueLiteral treats ?? and || as value positions but NOT &&, so data-testid={cond && 'my-id'} is silently dropped from the shared registry. assertIdShapes catches bad shapes, never a DROP, so the failure is invisible.

classifyAll runs isViteDevAsset over the WHOLE detail string while isHarnessNoise first extracts the URL, so a PRODUCT-url failure whose text merely contains a dev-asset-shaped substring sets the cell's corroboration flag without being muted itself — the corroboration signal is looser than the mute it authorises.

originAlive never consumes/cancels the response body (~144 undrained gallery-HTML responses per crawl under undici), and watchOrigin.stop() clears the timer without aborting an in-flight probe — so a genuine origin death detected on the final sample is discarded because stop() already snapshotted state.

lockPath() falls back to the literal 'win' when process.getuid is absent, so a shared-TEMP Windows/CI configuration gives all users one unlinkable lock file. os.userInfo().username works on every platform.
